items.title: Bytecode compilation can fail with "too many open files" on default Ubuntu settings
items.reason: This is the motivating issue for automatic limit adjustment and was closed by astral-sh/uv#17464. It concerns the inverse symptom—uv exhausting a low limit during bytecode compilation—not subprocess slowdown, but establishes why uv began raising RLIMIT_NOFILE.

items.title: Adjust the process ulimit to the maximum allowed on startup
items.reason: This introduced the exact limit-raising behavior behind the report. Its description acknowledged risks from increased limits and initially gated the behavior behind preview; its review explicitly noted that programs iterating over all possible file descriptors can time out. It did not report the tcsh/csh regression itself.

items.title: uv 0.12 preview stabilization tracking issue
items.reason: This is the canonical uv 0.12 stabilization discussion. Maintainers specifically considered whether adjust-ulimit had caused problems before deciding to stabilize it; astral-sh/uv#20225 closed the tracker.

items.title: Stabilize preview features for uv 0.12
items.reason: This made adjust-ulimit the default for uv 0.12, matching the reported regression boundary. The PR raises the open-file limit at startup but contains no tcsh/csh-specific report or remedy.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests using literal terms including adjust-ulimit, RLIMIT_NOFILE, NOFILE, ulimit, tcsh, csh, setrlimit, UV_NO_ULIMIT, close file descriptors, and open file limit. Conceptual searches covered inherited child/subprocess resource limits, uv run startup slowdown, programs scanning descriptor ranges, and excessive open files; fix-oriented searches followed the preview implementation and uv 0.12 stabilization chain. No earlier tracker for the tcsh/csh slowdown or an opt-out was found. Plausible adjacent candidates were ruled out: astral-sh/uv#11296 concerns uv exhausting a low limit in huge workspaces, astral-sh/uv#17512 concerns uv retaining many live cache-lock descriptors, and astral-sh/uv#6105 concerns older QEMU bytecode timeouts rather than raised inherited limits.

type_reason: This is a newly reported performance regression, not a duplicate: no existing issue or pull request tracks the tcsh/csh slowdown. Repository source confirms that uv raises the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE to the hard limit subject to a 1,048,576 cap, states that child processes inherit it, and warns that code iterating over every possible descriptor can time out. astral-sh/uv#20225 made that behavior default in uv 0.12, matching the reported onset. The reporter's tcsh implementation details and exact 100x measurement were not independently confirmed from this repository, but the source-backed behavior and reproducible version-specific degradation establish incorrect behavior appropriate for the bug label.
summary: No prior tracker covers this specific regression. The closest history is the low-limit failure that motivated adjust-ulimit, its preview implementation, and its stabilization as the uv 0.12 default.
